A carrier 1 % off is not a carrier. A gap 3 % long is
still a gap a receiver calls a zero - which is why
the CARRIER is the quantity fitted to the clock and
the GAPS are the quantities fitted to microseconds,
and why they are not fitted the same way.

The burst is IDENTICAL for both values, so the value is
carried entirely by the silence. The bit is the rotating
copy's own bit 0 and the copy is rotated right after each
slot, so there is no shifting to get wrong.

the check the mutation gate forced into the TB
"Each half is constant" IS NOT "the two halves are EQUAL".
The gate's first run had three survivors of eleven. One put BOTH half periods
on the same delay pair, which produced a carrier of 788 clocks one way and 782
38.05 kHz against 37.88, 0.4 % asymmetric on every edge
inside every frequency window a real receiver has - and it PASSED.
A receiver does not care that the carrier is on frequency. It cares that the
carrier is a CARRIER, and one whose halves differ is a square wave at 38 kHz
with the wrong duty cycle. So the TB now measures the two DISTRIBUTIONS
, to within a clock, and that check is the act's
The other two survivors were a burst of 20 carrier cycles (526 us, -6.4 %,
which the old +/-10 % window accepted - now +/-5 %, which admits the two widths
a whole number of cycles can produce, 21 at -1.7 % and 22 at +2.9 %, and
rejects the third) and a mutant that was BEHAVIOURALLY A NO-OP because its
anchor was written against the byte's LOAD rather than its ROTATE.
A "whole number of carrier cycles" check was written and then DELETED as
unsound. The burst opens with a two-instruction initiation pulse, so its
span is not a whole number of periods - and the check fired on all ten bursts
A check that is wrong about what it measures is worse than no check: the first
thing anyone would do is loosen the tolerance until it went away, and then the
loosened tolerance is the one that is believed.
